title: Same-Origin Policy
body:
The browser's default security rule: JavaScript running on one [[Origin]] cannot read data from a different origin. In the venue analogy, staff from Venue A can't look inside Venue B's booth.

The critical detail that gets asked in interviews: this is enforced **entirely by your browser, never by the server**. The server has no idea it's happening. In many cases the request is still sent, still reaches their machine, and still executes — the database write happens — and only the *response* is withheld from your JS. That asymmetry is exactly why [[CSRF]] is a real attack: the policy blocks reading, not sending.

[[CORS]] is the mechanism by which a server can opt out of this restriction for specific origins, and [[Preflight Request]] is how the browser checks before certain requests.
